output.brief:
The most likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads or the hills. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans while your in-house bay was closed. Eleven of them used fluid from an old bulk drum that had lost its cap and had absorbed water. That drum ran dry on 9 September. Those same 11 vans account for all 27 complaints. Two were tested on 24 September and the fluid boiled at about 150°C, against 255°C for fresh stock. Your drivers use those vans and other vans on the same Upper Wend routes. They report no problems in the other vans. So the hills are only where the fault shows up.

What to do this week: pull the other 9 vans from the bay-3 drum (the 11, minus LK-217 and LK-224, which were already renewed) and test and renew their fluid from sealed stock. Also check LK-214 and LK-227, which got new-drum fluid, plus the vans Calder Road serviced, as a precaution. Do not issue warnings. Complaints were accurate, and punishing them would stop reports. Hold off on changing pad supplier. The squeal data can't separate new pads from the new brand. Northfield's 25 September advice got no reply, so find out why. I'm fairly confident, around 90%.
